items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: I'll save my dear friend Gene Krupa for later.

ctx.x: And I adapted to tuning my drums along those lines, and still adhere to those sounds today. I can't stand a deep snare drum's tone. That's why I use a three and a half, or at the most, a four-inch deep snare. I like the four-inch by 13-inch in diameter, the so-called piccolo snare drum in my work -- I've been using it for a long time for a crisp sound.

I'll save my dear friend Gene Krupa for later. His part in the drumming world is a legend in itself -- not only as a playing artist, but in the breaking down of old traditions and the drum's importance in bands. The huge growth of drum equipment and sales is an outgrowth of

his association with Benny Goodman. Benny Goodman's entrance into the jazz picture from '35 on, I only mention this -- not to deviate from my personal story, but because all of us drummers in the jazz era were affected in some way of another by his predominance. A legend in his time, without peer.
